pages.text: The Akaishi Generator Matrix is a sealed-chamber multiblock that burns fuel at a fixed multiplier.$(br2)$(bold)Structure:$(reset)$(li)Build a closed box from Generator Matrix Casings; the shell is an odd-sized hollow box$(li)Mount the Matrix Controller in a wall$(li)Mount an Energy Output Port and a Fuel Input Port$(li)The interior must be completely empty$(br2)An unsealed box does not function; breaking any casing shuts it down immediately.$(br2)Two shell sizes exist: 3×3×3 (Basic) and 5×5×5 (Advanced). The controller block installed determines the tier.

The $(bold)Basic Generator Matrix$(reset) is a sealed 3×3×3 shell.$(br2)$(bold)Formed stats:$(reset)$(li)Output multiplier: $(bold)×45$(reset)$(li)Generation: $(bold)3375 AE/tick$(reset)$(li)Energy storage: $(bold)5 million$(reset)$(li)Fuel coefficient ×9/8: the same fuel yields approximately 1.13× more power$(br2)An Energy Output Port must be installed in the wall; it provides a $(bold)100 million$(reset) buffer that supplies the grid.$(br2)Build instructions are in the $(l:akaishi:matrix)Matrix Structures$(/l) entry.

The $(bold)Advanced Generator Matrix$(reset) is a sealed 5×5×5 shell.$(br2)$(bold)Formed stats:$(reset)$(li)Output multiplier: $(bold)×200$(reset)$(li)Generation: $(bold)15000 AE/tick$(reset)$(li)Energy storage: $(bold)50 million$(reset)$(li)Fuel coefficient ×9/4: the same fuel yields approximately 2.25× more power$(br2)Both tiers share the Fuel Input Port, which buffers 27 stacks and feeds the controller automatically (item-pipe compatible); upgrade components increase output further.$(br2)For higher output, use the $(l:akaishi:reactor)Reactor$(/l) and the $(l:akaishi:fusion)Fusion Reactor$(/l).

Reading order: $(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l) for fuels, then connect $(l:akaishi:energy_pipe)Energy Pipes$(/l) and $(l:akaishi:energy_cell)Energy Cells$(/l). The standalone $(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l) is the alternative for smaller lines. General multiblock layout rules are in $(l:akaishi:matrix)Matrix Structures$(/l).
